     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiCurve
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# The degree homomorphism on the Čech Picard group
    11	
    12	For the curve bundle `X` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over
    13	a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹` of the structure sheaf — the two instance hypotheses
    14	through which properness enters), this file builds the **degree homomorphism** on the Čech
    15	Picard group and records the E-i..E-iii interface of the degree lane
    16	(`informal/degree-pic0-recon.md` §3 G-D3, `informal/deg-d2-meromorphic-worksheet.md` W5).
    17	
    18	The anchored class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K : X.CurveDivisor → X.CechPic` of the
    19	meromorphic bridge (`Picard/DivisorClassMeromorphic.lean`) is surjective, with fibres the
    20	principal divisors. The degree of a Weil divisor is class-invariant: two divisors of equal
    21	class differ by a principal divisor (extraction `(X)`, `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`)
    22	and principal divisors have degree zero (`deg_divOf`, the χ-ledger), so `deg` descends to a
    23	homomorphism on classes.
    24	
    25	## Main declarations
    26	
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg` — the degree homomorphism `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`:
    28	  `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D` for any Weil divisor `D`. The carrier `Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`
    29	  is chosen so that a *value* `classDeg L` is a genuine integer: `X.CechPic` is a `CommGroup`
    30	  (line-bundle tensor) and the degrees form the additive group `ℤ`, so the idiomatic
    31	  packaging of "a group homomorphism from the multiplicative Picard group to the additive
    32	  group `ℤ`" is an `AddMonoidHom` out of `Additive X.CechPic`. Because `Additive X.CechPic`
    33	  is definitionally `X.CechPic`, the interface statements below read literally, and
    34	  `map_zero`/`map_add`/`map_neg`/`map_zsmul` come for free from the bundled hom.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_picClass` (**E-i**, normalization): `classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`,
    36	  the definitional anchor, for *every* Weil divisor `D`.
    37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_mul` (**E-ii**, homomorphism):
    38	  `classDeg (L · L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'`.
    39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg` (**E-iii**, χ-connection):
    40	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + classDeg 𝒪(D)`.
    41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: the Euler characteristic of a class
    42	  is well-defined — `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D'))` — via the multiplication
    43	  isomorphism `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` and `chi_congr` (no finiteness needed).
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_divisorClass`: the deg-D1 divisor class map has the same degree,
    45	  `classDeg (divisorClass K D) = deg D`, through the collapse `divisorClass_eq_picClass`.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg_curve`: the curve form
    47	  `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + classDeg 𝒪(D)` on the challenge curve.
    48	
    49	The recon's E-i pushforward-rank reading (`classDeg 𝒪(D) = dim_K Γ(𝒪_D)` for *effective*
    50	`D`, the Dedekind colength of the structure sheaf of the subscheme `D`) is a separate
    51	statement about global sections of `𝒪_D`; it is *not* this brick's definitional anchor
    52	(`classDeg 𝒪(D) = deg D`) and is deferred to a later node.
    53	-/
    54	
    55	set_option autoImplicit false
    56	
    57	universe u
    58	
    59	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    60	
    61	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    62	
    63	open Scheme
    64	
    65	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    66	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    67	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    69	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    70	
    71	/-! ## χ of a class is well-defined (no finiteness hypotheses) -/
    72	
    73	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    74	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
    75	/-- **The Euler characteristic of a Čech Picard class is well-defined**: Weil divisors of
    76	equal class have the same `χ(𝒪(D))`. If `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D')` then `D − D' = div g` for a rational
    77	function `g` (extraction `(X)`), and multiplication by `g` is an isomorphism of divisor
    78	sheaves `𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D − div g) = 𝒪(D')` (`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`), so the Euler
    79	characteristics agree by `chi_congr`. Needs no finiteness hypotheses. -/
    80	theorem chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    81	    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    82	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) = Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D') := by
    83	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h
    84	  have hD' : D - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g = D' := by
    85	    rw [← hg]; abel
    86	  have hiso := mulEquivDivisorSheaf K g D
    87	  rw [hD'] at hiso
    88	  exact Sheaf.chi_congr hiso
    89	
    90	/-! ## Well-definedness of the degree -/
    91	
    92	/-- **Well-definedness of the degree**: Weil divisors of equal Čech Picard class have equal
    93	degree. The class difference is a principal divisor `div g` (extraction `(X)`), and principal
    94	divisors have degree zero (`deg_divOf`, the χ-ledger). -/
    95	theorem deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    96	    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    97	    CurveDivisor.deg K D = CurveDivisor.deg K D' := by
    98	  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h
    99	  have hzero : CurveDivisor.deg K (D - D') = 0 := by
   100	    rw [hg]; exact deg_divOf K g
   101	  have hsub : CurveDivisor.deg K (D - D')
   102	      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - CurveDivisor.deg K D' := by
   103	    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, CurveDivisor.deg_add, CurveDivisor.deg_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg]
   104	  omega
   105	
   106	/-! ## The underlying degree function -/
   107	
   108	/-- The underlying function of the degree homomorphism: the degree of any Weil divisor
   109	realizing the class (`CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq`). Well-defined by
   110	`deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq`; bundled as `classDeg`. -/
   111	private noncomputable def classDegFun (L : X.CechPic) : ℤ :=
   112	  CurveDivisor.deg K (CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L).choose
   113	
   114	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   115	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
   116	/-- The chosen divisor realizes the class it was picked for. -/
   117	private theorem picClass_classDegFun_choose (L : X.CechPic) :
   118	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L).choose = L :=
   119	  (CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L).choose_spec
   120	
   121	/-- The degree function evaluates a divisor's own class to its degree. -/
   122	private theorem classDegFun_picClass (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   123	    classDegFun K (CurveDivisor.picClass K D) = CurveDivisor.deg K D :=
   124	  deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq K
   125	    (picClass_classDegFun_choose K (CurveDivisor.picClass K D))
   126	
   127	/-- The degree function vanishes on the trivial class. -/
   128	private theorem classDegFun_one : classDegFun K (1 : X.CechPic) = 0 := by
   129	  rw [← CurveDivisor.picClass_zero K, classDegFun_picClass, CurveDivisor.deg_zero]
   130	
   131	/-- The degree function turns the Picard product into a sum. -/
   132	private theorem classDegFun_mul (L L' : X.CechPic) :
   133	    classDegFun K (L * L') = classDegFun K L + classDegFun K L' := by
   134	  obtain ⟨D, rfl⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
   135	  obtain ⟨D', rfl⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L'
   136	  rw [← CurveDivisor.picClass_add, classDegFun_picClass, classDegFun_picClass,
   137	    classDegFun_picClass, CurveDivisor.deg_add]
   138	
   139	/-! ## The degree homomorphism -/
   140	
   141	/-- **The degree homomorphism on the Čech Picard group.** For the curve bundle `X`, the
   142	degree of a Weil divisor descends to a group homomorphism `classDeg K : Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ`
   143	on Picard classes: `classDeg K 𝒪(D) = deg K D`. Well-defined because equal classes differ by
   144	a principal divisor and principal divisors have degree zero (`deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq`).
   145	
   146	The value `classDeg K L` is a genuine integer (`Additive X.CechPic` is definitionally
   147	`X.CechPic`), so E-i (`classDeg_picClass`) and E-ii (`classDeg_mul`) read as literal integer
   148	equalities. The full `AddMonoidHom` API (`map_zero`, `map_add`, `map_neg`, `map_zsmul`) is
   149	available on `classDeg K`. -/
   150	noncomputable def classDeg : Additive X.CechPic →+ ℤ where
   151	  toFun L := classDegFun K L
   152	  map_zero' := classDegFun_one K
   153	  map_add' L L' := classDegFun_mul K L L'
   154	
   155	/-- **(E-i) Normalization** (the definitional anchor): the degree of the class `𝒪(D)` of a
   156	Weil divisor `D` is `deg D`, for *every* `D`. -/
   157	theorem classDeg_picClass (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   158	    classDeg K (CurveDivisor.picClass K D) = CurveDivisor.deg K D :=
   159	  classDegFun_picClass K D
   160	
   161	/-- **(E-ii) Homomorphism property**: the degree of a product of Picard classes is the sum of
   162	the degrees, `classDeg (L · L') = classDeg L + classDeg L'`. Immediate from `map_add` of the
   163	bundled `classDeg`; stated on the multiplicative Picard product for direct use. -/
   164	theorem classDeg_mul (L L' : X.CechPic) :
   165	    classDeg K (L * L') = classDeg K L + classDeg K L' :=
   166	  classDegFun_mul K L L'
   167	
   168	/-- The degree of the trivial class is zero. -/
   169	@[simp]
   170	theorem classDeg_one : classDeg K (1 : X.CechPic) = 0 :=
   171	  classDegFun_one K
   172	
   173	/-- The degree of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
   174	theorem classDeg_inv (L : X.CechPic) : classDeg K (L⁻¹ : X.CechPic) = -classDeg K L := by
   175	  have h := classDeg_mul K L (L⁻¹ : X.CechPic)
   176	  rw [mul_inv_cancel, classDeg_one] at h
   177	  omega
   178	
   179	/-! ## The χ-connection -/
   180	
   181	/-- **(E-iii) The χ-connection**: the Euler characteristic of the class `𝒪(D)` is the Euler
   182	characteristic of the structure sheaf plus the degree of the class,
   183	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + classDeg 𝒪(D)`. A restatement of the landed χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf`
   184	through the E-i normalization `classDeg_picClass`. -/
   185	theorem chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   186	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D)
   187	      = Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + classDeg K (CurveDivisor.picClass K D) := by
   188	  rw [classDeg_picClass]
   189	  exact chi_divisorSheaf K D
   190	
   191	/-! ## Compatibility with the deg-D1 divisor class map -/
   192	
   193	/-- **Compatibility with `divisorClass`**: the deg-D1 divisor class map has the same degree,
   194	`classDeg (divisorClass K D) = deg D`, via the collapse `divisorClass_eq_picClass`. -/
   195	theorem classDeg_divisorClass (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
   196	    classDeg K (divisorClass K D) = CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
   197	  rw [divisorClass_eq_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
   198	
   199	end AlgebraicGeometry
   200	
   201	/-! ## The curve layer -/
   202	
   203	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   204	
   205	open Scheme
   206	
   207	section Curve
   208	
   209	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   210	
   211	/-- **The degree homomorphism on the challenge curve** (Riemann–Roch-lite, class form): for
   212	every Weil divisor `D` on the smooth proper geometrically-irreducible curve `C`, the Euler
   213	characteristic of `𝒪(D)` is `χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + classDeg 𝒪(D)`. The structure-sheaf
   214	finiteness hypotheses of the conditional ledger are discharged on the curve, so this carries
   215	no finiteness side conditions. -/
   216	theorem chi_divisorSheaf_classDeg_curve (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   217	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   218	    (D : C.left.CurveDivisor) :
   219	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
   220	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
   221	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   222	    haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
   223	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   224	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   225	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
   226	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   227	      moduleFinite_hModule_one C
   228	    Sheaf.chi (C.left.divisorSheaf k D)
   229	      = 1 - genus C + classDeg k (CurveDivisor.picClass k D) := by
   230	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
   231	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
   232	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
   233	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
   234	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
   235	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
   236	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
   237	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
   238	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
   239	  rw [classDeg_picClass]
   240	  exact chi_divisorSheaf_curve C D
   241	
   242	end Curve
   243	
   244	end AlgebraicGeometry

(Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) := by
  have hPinf : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) := fun h => hP h.1
  rw [chi_sub_chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov E (pointDivisor P + E),
    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k U₀ hP E,
    sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) hPinf E]
  ring

/-- **Off the overlap, the bump at one step is equivalent to the one-chart step being full.**

For `P.point ∉ U₀`, the bump statement `χ(1·P+E) = χ(E) + [κ(P):k]` holds if and only if
the `U₁`-chart section space grows by exactly `[κ(P):k]`.  Neither direction needs an
exactness hypothesis.

**Read the quantifiers.**  This is an equivalence at a *single* `(P, E)`.  It does **not** say
`hbump` is consistent: `hbump` asserts the left side for *all* `E`, hence at every stage of the
tower `n·P`, and §5 shows the right side must fail for large `n` because `Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜` is
frozen there.  An earlier docstring here drew the consistency conclusion from this iff; that
inference is invalid, and `not_bump_of_notMem_left` is the correction. -/
theorem bump_iff_chartStep_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ E)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ E)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) E)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ (pointDivisor P + E))]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E))]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) (pointDivisor P + E))] :
    chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P ↔
      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ (pointDivisor P + E)) : ℤ)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ E) = residueDeg k P := by
  have h := chi_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem_left k U₀ U₁ hcov hP E
  omega

/-! ## §5. `hbump` is refuted off a chart — unconditionally

This section supersedes the reading this file shipped with, and it is the sharp answer to the
question inbox `I-0456` posed ("*where* is the hypothesis false?").

The mechanism is the **tower** `n·P`.  Fix `P.point ∉ U₀`.  Then along `E ↦ n·P + E`:

* `Γ(U₀, −)` is frozen — the point is off `U₀` (`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem`);
* `𝒜 = Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁, −)` is frozen — the point is off the overlap too;
* `Γ(U₁, −) ⊆ 𝒜` always, since `sectionSub` is antitone in the open.

So all three terms of `chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap` are bounded, giving `χ(n·P + E) ≤ dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(E))`
for **every** `n`.  But `hbump` forces `χ(n·P) = χ(0) + n·[κ(P):k]`, and `[κ(P):k] ≥ 1`
(`one_le_residueDeg`).  Linear growth against a fixed bound is a contradiction.

Credit: found by an adversarial `work-reviewer` audit of this module (inbox `I-0467`/`I-0468`),
which caught this file's own docstrings claiming the opposite.  I verified the argument
independently before landing it. -/

section BumpRefutedOffChart

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X]

/-- **An open missing `P` sees no change along the whole tower `n·P`.**  Iterate
`sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem`. -/
theorem sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem (U : X.Opens)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U) (E : X.WeilDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    sectionSub k U (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E) = sectionSub k U E := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp only [List.replicate_zero, divisorOfList, zero_add]
  | succ m ih =>
    rw [List.replicate_succ]
    simp only [divisorOfList]
    rw [show pointDivisor P + divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + E
          = pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + E) by abel,
      sectionSub_add_pointDivisor_of_notMem k U hP, ih]

variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **χ is BOUNDED along a tower at a point off one chart.**  `χ(n·P + E) ≤ dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(E))`
for every `n`, when `P.point ∉ U₀`.

Two of the three Čech terms are frozen by the tower and the third is trapped under the
overlap term (`Γ(U₁,−) ⊆ 𝒜`, antitonicity in the open).  No exactness hypothesis. -/
theorem chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    (n : ℕ) :
    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ E) : ℤ) := by
  have hPinf : P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) := fun h => hP h.1
  set D := divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E with hD
  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D
  have hle : Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
      ≤ Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) :=
    Submodule.finrank_mono (sectionSub_antitone_open k inf_le_right D)
  have h0 : sectionSub k U₀ D = sectionSub k U₀ E := by
    rw [hD]; exact sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem k U₀ hP E n
  rw [h0] at h
  omega

/-- **Chart-level finiteness alone forbids Riemann growth: `ℓ` is BOUNDED along a tower.**

`ℓ(n·P + E) ≤ dim Γ(U₀, 𝒪(E))` for every `n`, whenever `P.point ∉ U₀` and the `U₀`-chart
section spaces are finite-dimensional.  No cover hypothesis, no χ, no exactness datum: it is
`sectionSub k ⊤ D ≤ sectionSub k U₀ D` (antitonicity in the open) composed with the freeze.

**This is the root cause of everything in §5–§6, and it is worth stating separately because it is
stronger and simpler than the χ-level statements.**  Riemann–Roch says `ℓ(D)` grows like
`deg D`; this says it *cannot*, along any tower at a point missing a chart whose sections are
finite-dimensional.  So `Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)` at a **non-total** `U` is not
bookkeeping — it is a substantive geometric restriction, and any theorem assuming it over all
divisors has already excluded the curves Riemann–Roch is about.

Consequence for reading this whole module: the `[∀ D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k Uᵢ D)]`
binders on §5–§6 are what make the refutations available, and a consumer who supplies them for
convenience has chosen the geometry.  Found by a fresh-context review of this module. -/
theorem ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ : X.Opens)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀) (E : X.WeilDivisor)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] (n : ℕ) :
    ell k (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ E) := by
  have hsub : sectionSub k ⊤ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E)
      ≤ sectionSub k U₀ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + E) :=
    sectionSub_antitone_open k le_top _
  rw [sectionSub_divisorOfList_replicate_of_notMem k U₀ hP E n] at hsub
  exact Submodule.finrank_mono hsub

/-- **`hbump` IS FALSE whenever some prime divisor sits off one chart of the cover.**

Unconditional: no `chi_add`, no exactness hypothesis, no approximation input.  `hbump` forces
`χ` to grow linearly along the tower `n·P` while `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` bounds it,
so `hbump` cannot hold.

**This is inbox `I-0449`'s conclusion, strengthened.**  That audit derived the same
incompatibility *conditionally*, from `ChiLedger.chi_add`'s conclusion; an earlier version of
this module claimed on that basis that the audit had measured `chi_add` rather than `hbump`.
The claim was false and is retracted here in Lean rather than only in prose.

Note the reach: `P.point ∉ U₀` (or symmetrically `∉ U₁`) is far weaker than `P.point ∉ U₀ ⊓ U₁`,
so this refutes `hbump` on a *larger* set of primes than `I-0449` addressed.  Together with
`LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump` — which derives the closed ledger *from* `hbump` — the honest
consequence is that the bump route to the ledger is dead for any cover having such a prime,
and consumers must not be pointed at it. -/
theorem not_bump_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
    ¬ (∀ (Q : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
        chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor Q + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k Q) := by
  intro hbump
  have hgrow : ∀ n : ℕ,
      chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + (0 : X.WeilDivisor))
        = chi k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor) + n * residueDeg k P := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero => simp only [List.replicate_zero, divisorOfList]; ring_nf; rfl
    | succ m ih =>
      rw [List.replicate_succ]
      simp only [divisorOfList]
      rw [show pointDivisor P + divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + (0 : X.WeilDivisor)
            = pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList (List.replicate m P) + (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) by abel,
        hbump P, ih]
      push_cast; ring
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt
    ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) : ℤ)
      - chi k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor))
  have hb := chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower k U₀ U₁ hcov hP (0 : X.WeilDivisor) n
  rw [hgrow n] at hb
  have hr : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (residueDeg k P : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast one_le_residueDeg k P
  have hnn : (n : ℤ) ≤ n * residueDeg k P := by nlinarith [Int.natCast_nonneg n]
  omega

end BumpRefutedOffChart

/-! ## §3. Cluster-P consequences that no longer need the ledger

The two statements cluster P actually wants downstream are a **section lower bound**
(Riemann inequality) and an **H¹ vanishing criterion**.  Both follow from the ungated χ
formula without `hledger`, `hbump`, or any exactness hypothesis.  What they still need is
the *geometric* input relating the chart dimensions to `deg D`; that input is isolated as
an explicit hypothesis rather than hidden, and it is the honest residual leaf. -/

/-- **Riemann inequality, gate-free.**  `ℓ(D) ≥ χ(D)` is elementary (`chi_le_ell`), so the
ungated χ formula turns any lower bound on the Čech count into a lower bound on `ℓ(D)`:

`dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) ≤ ℓ(D)`.

Compare `SectionBounds.degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell` and
`BoundedVanishing.exists_bound_ell_eq`, which reach comparable conclusions only under
`hledger`.  Here there is no ledger hypothesis at all; the content has moved into the
computable left-hand side. -/
theorem charts_sub_overlap_le_ell (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
    (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
      + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
      - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := by
  rw [← chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D]
  exact chi_le_ell k U₀ U₁ D

/-- **H¹ vanishing is equivalent to the Čech count being exact** — no gate.

`Ȟ¹(D) = 0` iff `dim Γ(U₀,𝒪(D)) + dim Γ(U₁,𝒪(D)) − dim 𝒜(D) = ℓ(D)`, i.e. iff the
inclusion–exclusion count computes `ℓ(D)` on the nose.

This is the vanishing criterion cluster P needs, and unlike
`BoundedVanishing.subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` (a restatement of `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`) it is a
**numerical** criterion: it can be certified by counting dimensions on the two charts,
which is what an explicit cover computation actually produces.  Note it is a genuine
two-way reduction, not a reformulation of `h1dim = 0` — the right-hand side mentions only
the three chart dimensions and `ℓ`.

**Caveat.**  This is a criterion, not a vanishing theorem: nothing here or elsewhere in AJC
proves its right-hand side at any curve.  Do not read it as closing single-field vanishing.

It is *not*, however, damaged by §5–§6: this statement assumes finiteness at the single divisor
`D` only, and its right-hand side compares the count with `ℓ(D)` rather than with `deg_k D`, so
the tower argument does not touch it (see the discussion at
`exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero_of_charts`).  Vanishing content survives; it is the ledger's *growth*
claim that the chart-finiteness binders refute. -/
theorem h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (D : X.WeilDivisor)
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)] [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)] :
    h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 ↔
      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ) := by
  have h := chi_eq_charts_sub_overlap k U₀ U₁ hcov D
  rw [chi] at h
  omega

/-- **Uniform vanishing from a uniform chart count.**  If above some weighted-degree
threshold `b` the Čech count is exact at every divisor, then `h¹` vanishes uniformly above
`b`.  The quantifier structure is the one cluster P's consumers take, and the hypothesis is
now a statement about chart dimensions rather than about a connecting homomorphism.

This is deliberately stated with the finiteness binders as an instance-quantified
hypothesis, matching `ResidueField.UniformlyBoundedVanishing`'s shape, so that a consumer
proving the chart count over a family of divisors gets uniform vanishing directly.

**Is `hcount` refutable by the §5–§6 tower argument?  No — and the reason is the useful part.**
This hypothesis equates the chart count with `ℓ(D)`, and `ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` says
`ℓ` is *also* bounded along the tower under these binders.  Bounded = bounded is no
contradiction, so unlike `hledger` — which equates χ with the **unbounded** `deg_k D` — `hcount`
survives the tower.

That contrast is the sharpest available statement of what went wrong with the lane's ledger:
`hcount` and `hledger` both look like "the Čech count is exact", but only the ledger asserts
*growth*.  The vanishing content is safe; the Riemann-growth content is what these binders
forbid.  So this theorem is not vacuous for that reason — though it remains a criterion, proved
at no curve, and it does carry the `∀ D` chart-finiteness binders, which by the module header
already restrict the geometry. -/
theorem exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero_of_charts (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤) (b : ℤ)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    (hcount : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
      (Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ D) : ℤ)
        + Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₁ D)
        - Module.finrank k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = (ell k D : ℤ)) :
    ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 :=
  fun D hD => (h1dim_eq_zero_iff_charts k U₀ U₁ hcov D).mpr (hcount D hD)

end ChiCharts

/-! ## §6. The closed ledger itself is refuted on such a cover — so the leaf needs a better cover

An earlier §4 of this module defined `ChartCountsDegree` (verbatim the closed ledger) and
derived `deg_k(div g) = 0` from it, advertised as "the principal-divisor leaf with the ledger
removed".  **Both the framing and the theorem have been deleted**, for two independent reasons
found by the audit at inbox `I-0467`:

1. It was a *duplicate*, not a reduction.  `ChartCountsDegree` was `Iff.rfl` to `hledger`, and
   `SectionBounds.degK_principal_eq_zero` already accepts that hypothesis verbatim — so the new
   theorem was the old one with a renamed hypothesis.  Admitting in a docstring that a
   restatement is a restatement does not make it worth adding; `I-0456`'s lesson is to delete or
   fold, not to relabel.
2. It was *vacuous on the covers this file is about*.  `ledger_refuted_of_notMem_left` below
   shows the ledger is outright false whenever a prime divisor lies off one chart — the same
   tower argument as §5, since `deg_k` grows linearly along `n·P` while χ stays bounded.

What survives is sharper than what was deleted, and it is a genuine constraint on the route
rather than a theorem about it. -/

section LedgerRefuted

variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- **The closed ledger is FALSE if any prime divisor lies off one chart of the cover.**

`deg_k` grows linearly along the tower `n·P` (it is additive with
`deg_k P = [κ(P):k] ≥ 1`), while `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` bounds χ there.  So
`χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` cannot hold at every `D`.

**Consequence for the lane — with the quantifiers stated exactly, because they matter.**  Every
conditional statement in `SectionBounds.lean` §3, `BoundedVanishing.lean` and
`GlobalGeneration.lean` takes this same `hledger`.  Where those consumers *also* satisfy this
theorem's two extra hypotheses, their `hledger` is unsatisfiable and they are vacuous.

The two extra hypotheses are **not** automatic, and it would be an overclaim to drop them:

* `hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`.  The consumers do **not** assume it — they are stated for arbitrary
  `U₀ U₁`.  Without a cover, `chi` is not computing a Čech Euler characteristic and this
  argument says nothing.
* the three `∀ D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k · D)` instances.  The consumers assume finiteness
  only at `⊤` (`Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)`), never at the charts.  As the module header
  notes, chart-level finiteness at a non-total open is a real restriction — it is what forbids
  Riemann growth along the tower.

So the honest statement is: **on a genuine two-chart cover whose chart section spaces are all
finite-dimensional, and which has a prime divisor off a chart, the ledger is false and the lane's
conditional results are vacuous.** Whether a given curve's cover meets that description is not
settled here. What *is* settled is that the bump route cannot be repaired by supplying
approximation data: on such a cover there is nothing to supply. The fix is a different cover
hypothesis, or more charts. -/
theorem ledger_refuted_of_notMem_left (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
    {P : X.PrimeDivisor} (hP : P.point ∉ U₀)
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₀ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U₁ D)]
    [∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)]
    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
    ¬ (∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D) := by
  intro hledger
  have hdeg : ∀ n : ℕ, degK k (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + (0 : X.WeilDivisor))
      = n * residueDeg k P := by
    intro n
    rw [add_zero, degK_divisorOfList]
    simp [List.map_replicate, List.sum_replicate]
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := exists_nat_gt
    ((Module.finrank k (sectionSub k U₀ (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) : ℤ)
      - chi k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor))
  have hb := chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower k U₀ U₁ hcov hP (0 : X.WeilDivisor) n
  rw [hledger (divisorOfList (List.replicate n P) + (0 : X.WeilDivisor)), hdeg n] at hb
  have hr : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (residueDeg k P : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast one_le_residueDeg k P
  have hnn : (n : ℤ) ≤ n * residueDeg k P := by nlinarith [Int.natCast_nonneg n]
  omega

end LedgerRefuted

end Adelic

/-!
# The P2 cohomology kit: `h⁰`, `h¹`, `χ` on a 2-affine Čech cover

For a scheme `C` over a base
ring `k` (structure morphism `C.hom : C.left ⟶ Spec k`; in the intended
application `k` is a field, but the carrier layer is stated over any
commutative ring, so the same kit serves noetherian bases), a sheaf of modules
`M : C.left.Modules`, and a bundled 2-affine Mayer–Vietoris cover
`S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare`, this file upgrades the `AddMonoidHom`-level
Čech vocabulary `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff` /
`AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok` (`Picard/RigidPushforward.lean`) to
`k`-linear form and defines the numerical invariants:

* `Scheme.BaseSections C M U` — the sections `Γ(M, U)` as a `k`-module, the
  `k`-structure being restriction of scalars along the structure ring map
  `k → Γ(C, U)` (`toModuleKSheaf.kToSection`, the same scalar path as the
  sheaf-of-`k`-modules dialect `toModuleKSheaf`, so the two dialects agree on
  the nose for the structure sheaf).  The module-instance path is pinned
  ONCE, on this type synonym: `Module.compHom` along `kToSection C (op U)`.
* `AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ` — the difference-of-restrictions map as
  a `k`-linear map (same underlying function as `moduleSectionDiff`);
* `AffineCoverMVSquare.H0ₗ` (kernel submodule), `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cokₗ`
  (cokernel `k`-module, same underlying group as `moduleH1Cok`);
* `AffineCoverMVSquare.h0`, `.h1` (`Module.finrank`s), `.chi := h0 - h1`.

**Cover discipline.**  All invariants are pinned **on a chosen
cover `S`**.  Cover-independence is deliberately out of scope here:
it is to be discharged Čech-to-Čech (comparing two 2-affine covers through
their common refinement, exactly as `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve` compares
Čech to derived `H¹` through the Mayer–Vietoris `(0,1)`-slice) — **never**
through the `HasCechToHModuleIso` comparison gate, which remains
instance-free.  For `H⁰` cover-independence is already trivial and proved
here (`globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ`: the kernel is the global sections, by the
sheaf condition); for `H¹` of the structure sheaf it is inherited from the
gate-free derived comparison (`hModuleOneEquivH1Cokₗ_unit` below, both sides

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

/-! ## §1. Sections of a sheaf of modules as modules over the base ring

The base-ring structure on `Γ(M, U)` comes from the structure morphism
`C.hom : C.left ⟶ Spec k` through the per-open structure ring map
`toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (op U) : k →+* Γ(C, U)`
(`Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf.lean`) — the SAME scalar path as
the sheaf-of-`k`-modules dialect `toModuleKSheaf`, which is what makes the
`𝒪_C` comparison below definitional.  The instance path is pinned once, on
the type synonym `BaseSections`. -/

section BaseSections

variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]

/-- The sections `Γ(M, U)` of a sheaf of modules `M` on a `k`-scheme `C`,
as a module over the base ring `k` (type synonym; the `k`-module instance
below is restriction of scalars along the structure ring map
`k → Γ(C, U)`).  The scheme is carried as an object `C : Over (Spec k)` so
that the structure morphism — hence the `k`-action — is part of the data. -/
@[nolint unusedArguments]
def BaseSections (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
    (U : C.left.Opens) : Type u :=
  Γ(M, U)

noncomputable instance (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : C.left.Modules)
    (U : C.left.Opens) : AddCommGroup (BaseSections C M U) :=
  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup Γ(M, U))

/-- The per-open structure ring map `k →+* Γ(C, U)` of a `k`-scheme `C`,
respelled on the scheme-sections notation `Γ(C.left, U)` (so that the
tautological module instance `Module Γ(C.left, U) Γ(M, U)` is keyed
correctly).  Definitional: it IS `toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (op U)`
(`baseRingMap_eq_kToSection`), the scalar path of the sheaf-of-`k`-modules
    (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M inf_le_right).comp (LinearMap.snd k _ _)

/-- The value of the `k`-linear difference map. -/
lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_apply (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) (p : BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂) :
    S.sectionDiffₗ C M p =
      (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₁)).op).hom p.1 -
        (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂ ≤ S.U₂)).op).hom p.2 :=
  rfl

/-- The `k`-linear difference map has the same underlying function as the
`AddMonoidHom`-level `moduleSectionDiff`; this is what transports every
statement about the additive kit to the `k`-linear kit and back. -/
lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_coe_moduleSectionDiff
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
    ⇑(S.sectionDiffₗ C M) = ⇑(S.moduleSectionDiff M) :=
  rfl

/-- **`H⁰` on the cover, as a submodule**: the kernel of the `k`-linear
difference map — pairs of sections agreeing on the overlap.  By the sheaf
condition this is the global sections (`globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ`), which is
why `h0` is honestly cover-independent already at this wave. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.H0ₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) :
    Submodule k (BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂) :=
  LinearMap.ker (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)

/-- **The concrete Čech `Ȟ¹` of the cover, as a `k`-module**: the cokernel
`Γ(U₁ ⊓ U₂, M) ⧸ im(sectionDiffₗ)`.  Same underlying abelian group as
`AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleH1Cok` (the ranges of `sectionDiffₗ` and
`moduleSectionDiff` coincide, `sectionDiffₗ_coe_moduleSectionDiff`). -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cokₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) : Type u :=
  BaseSections C M (S.U₁ ⊓ S.U₂) ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)

noncomputable instance (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
    AddCommGroup (S.H1Cokₗ C M) :=
  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)))

noncomputable instance (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
    Module k (S.H1Cokₗ C M) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Module k (_ ⧸ LinearMap.range (S.sectionDiffₗ C M)))

/-- **`h⁰(M)` on the cover `S`**: the `k`-dimension of the kernel of the
difference map (junk value `0` when infinite-dimensional; finiteness for
general coherent `M` is a later P2 wave). -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.h0 (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank k (S.H0ₗ C M)

/-- **`h¹(M)` on the cover `S`**: the `k`-dimension of the concrete Čech
cokernel (junk value `0` when infinite-dimensional). -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.h1 (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank k (S.H1Cokₗ C M)

/-- **The Euler characteristic `χ(M) = h⁰(M) − h¹(M)` on the cover `S`.**
It agrees with the sheaf-theoretic `χ` whenever both `h⁰` and `h¹` are finite
and the cover computes them, which for the curves considered here is every
2-affine cover. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.chi (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) : ℤ :=
  (S.h0 C M : ℤ) - (S.h1 C M : ℤ)

lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.chi_def (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) :
    S.chi C M = (S.h0 C M : ℤ) - (S.h1 C M : ℤ) :=
  rfl

end CechKit

/-! ## §3. `H⁰` is the global sections (sheaf gluing on the 2-cover)

The kernel of the difference map is `Γ(C, M)`: restriction into the pair is
injective (separatedness) and hits every agreeing pair (gluing), both through
the sheaf property of `M.presheaf` on the cover `{U₁, U₂}` of `⊤`.  This is
the trivial half of cover-independence, done at this wave because the `𝒪`
base case needs it. -/

section Gluing

variable {k : Type u} [CommRing k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

/-- The pair-of-restrictions map `Γ(M, ⊤) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₁, M) × Γ(U₂, M)`, the
`k`-linear upgrade of `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionRes`. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionResₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) :
    BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens) →ₗ[k]
      BaseSections C M S.U₁ × BaseSections C M S.U₂ :=
  (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M le_top).prod (BaseSections.restrictₗ C M le_top)

/-- The pair of restrictions of a global section agrees on the overlap: the
two-term complex property, `k`-linear form. -/
lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.sectionDiffₗ_sectionResₗ (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
    (M : C.left.Modules) (s : BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens)) :
    S.sectionDiffₗ C M (S.sectionResₗ C M s) = 0 := by
  have h := congrArg (fun f => f s) (S.moduleSectionDiff_comp_moduleSectionRes M)
  exact h

/-- The two-element indexed family `{U₁, U₂}` of a 2-affine cover square, used
to feed the Mathlib sheaf-condition API. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.pairFamily {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) : ULift.{u} Bool → X.Opens :=
  fun i => bif i.down then S.U₁ else S.U₂

lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.le_iSup_pairFamily {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare) : (⊤ : X.Opens) ≤ iSup S.pairFamily := by
  rw [← S.cover]
  exact sup_le (le_iSup S.pairFamily ⟨true⟩) (le_iSup S.pairFamily ⟨false⟩)

/-- **`H⁰ₗ` is the global sections.**  The corestriction of the
pair-of-restrictions map is a `k`-linear equivalence
`Γ(C, M) ≃ₗ[k] H⁰ₗ(S, M)`: injective by separatedness of the sheaf
`M.presheaf`, surjective onto the kernel by the gluing axiom, both on the
2-element cover `{U₁, U₂}` of `⊤`.  In particular `h0` does not depend on
the cover. -/
noncomputable def AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivH0ₗ
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) (M : C.left.Modules) :
    BaseSections C M (⊤ : C.left.Opens) ≃ₗ[k] S.H0ₗ C M :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective

field of constants `κ` (Λ-package instances + unconditional
`HasTrivialConstants`). -/
theorem AffineCoverMVSquare.h0_unit_baseChangeField_eq_one
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    (S.baseChangeField κ).h0 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.ringCatSheaf) = 1 :=
  (S.baseChangeField κ).h0_unit_eq_one (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)

/-- `h¹(𝒪_{C_κ}) = genus C_κ` on the base-changed cover — the base-changed
genus, at base field `κ` (the comparison with `genus C` is the P2/P3
flat-base-change item, NOT claimed here). -/
theorem AffineCoverMVSquare.h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    (S.baseChangeField κ).h1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.ringCatSheaf) =
      genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) :=
  (S.baseChangeField κ).h1_unit_eq_genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)

/-- `H⁰ₗ` of `𝒪` on the base-changed curve is a finite-dimensional `κ`-space. -/
instance module_finite_H0ₗ_unit_baseChangeField
    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    Module.Finite κ ((S.baseChangeField κ).H0ₗ (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.ringCatSheaf)) :=
  module_finite_H0ₗ_unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) (S.baseChangeField κ)

/-- `Ȟ¹ₗ` of `𝒪` on the base-changed curve is a finite-dimensional `κ`-space:
the Λ-package instances make `C_κ` an AJC curve over `κ`, so the unconditional
genus finiteness applies verbatim at base field `κ`. -/
instance module_finite_H1Cokₗ_unit_baseChangeField
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
    (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare) :
    Module.Finite κ ((S.baseChangeField κ).H1Cokₗ (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.ringCatSheaf)) :=
  module_finite_H1Cokₗ_unit (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) (S.baseChangeField κ)

end BaseChangeUnit

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeIsoTransport

     8	/-!
     9	# W7-B3: the degree is invariant along scheme isomorphisms (`classDeg_map_iso`)
    10	
    11	For an isomorphism `e : X ≅ Y` of curve bundles over one field `K`, the degree of a Čech
    12	Picard class is preserved by the contravariant transport `Scheme.CechPic.map e.hom.left`:
    13	
    14	`classDeg K (CechPic.map e.hom.left L) = classDeg K L`.
    15	
    16	This is `informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §3's named Wave-7 lemma **`classDeg_map_iso`** — the
    17	lighter sibling of E-iv-alg (`RiemannRoch/DegreeBaseFieldInvariance.lean`), built by the
    18	same ladder with the base-field transition `π` replaced by an isomorphism, so that every
    19	leg degenerates (`informal/w7-worksheet.md` §D2-iii, brick B-3): single-point reduction
    20	along `picClass` generators, tracked point equations, pullback presentation — and then the
    21	fiber is a *single* point, the coefficient is `ord` of the transported uniformizer
    22	(`= 1` by transport of the adic multiplicity along the stalk isomorphism, no colength),
    23	and the residue degree transports along the induced isomorphism of residue fields.
    24	
    25	## Main declarations
    26	
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_of_isIso` — the scheme-level engine: for an
    28	  isomorphism `f : W ⟶ X` over `Spec K`, `classDeg K (CechPic.map f L) = classDeg K L`.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_map_iso` — **the W7-B3 keystone**, the worksheet's pinned
    30	  `Over`-category form at `e : X ≅ Y` in `Over (Spec (.of K))` with the standing curve pack.
    31	
    32	The transport legs (adic-multiplicity/`ord` transport along the stalk isomorphism,
    33	`residueDeg_eq_of_isIso`, `overAlgebraMap_app`, and the generic pulled tracked point
    34	system `pointPullbackEquations` with its fiber computation) live in
    35	`RiemannRoch/DegreeIsoTransport.lean`.
    36	
    37	Consumers: W7-B4a (`degAt` matching through B-3 + E-iv-alg) and W7-B4b (θ); EW-3 of the
    38	Wave-7 recon is closed by this brick.
    39	-/
    40	
    41	set_option autoImplicit false
    42	
    43	universe u
    44	
    45	open CategoryTheory Limits UniqueFactorizationMonoid IsDedekindDomain
    46	
    47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    48	
    49	/-! ## The degenerate ladder: `classDeg` invariance along an isomorphism -/
    50	
    51	section Ladder
    52	
    53	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {W X : Scheme.{u}}
    54	  [W.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    55	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral W]
    56	  [QuasiCompact (W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    57	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    58	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    59	
    60	/-- **The pulled point divisor along an isomorphism is the single preimage point**: the
    61	divisor of the presentation of the pulled tracked point system has `K`-degree equal to the
    62	residue degree of `x'`. -/
    63	private theorem deg_presentationDivisor_pointPullback_of_isIso (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f]
    64	    (hover : f ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) = W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    65	    (hgen : f.base (genericPoint W) = genericPoint X)
    66	    {x' : X} (hx' : x' ≠ genericPoint X) :
    67	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
    68	        (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation)
    69	      = (X.residueDeg K x' : ℤ) := by
    70	  have hcoe : ⇑(Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso f)) = ⇑f.base := by
    71	    rw [Scheme.coe_homeoOfIso, asIso_hom]
    72	  have hinj : Function.Injective f.base := by
    73	    have h := (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso f)).injective
    74	    rwa [hcoe] at h
    75	  set z₀ : W := (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso f)).symm x' with hz₀def
    76	  have hfz₀ : f.base z₀ = x' := by
    77	    have h := (Scheme.homeoOfIso (asIso f)).apply_symm_apply x'
    78	    rwa [hcoe] at h
    79	  have hz₀ : z₀ ≠ genericPoint W := fun h => hx' (by rw [← hfz₀, h, hgen])
    80	  have hcoeff : ∀ (z : W) (hz : z ≠ genericPoint W),
    81	      coeffAt hz (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
    82	          (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation)
    83	        = Multiplicative.toAdd (Scheme.ordZ (W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    84	            ((pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation.elem z)) :=
    85	    fun z hz => Scheme.coeffAt_presentationDivisor K _ hz
    86	  have hzero : ∀ (z : W) (hz : z ≠ genericPoint W), z ≠ z₀ →
    87	      coeffAt hz (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
    88	        (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation) = 0 := by
    89	    intro z hz hne
    90	    have hfne : f.base z ≠ x' := fun h => hne (hinj (by rw [h, hfz₀]))
    91	    rw [hcoeff z hz, pointPullbackEquations_presentation_elem_of_ne K f hgen hx' hfne,
    92	      map_one, toAdd_one]
    93	  have hc1 : Multiplicative.toAdd (Scheme.ordZ (W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz₀
    94	      ((pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation.elem z₀)) = 1 := by
    95	    rw [pointPullbackEquations_presentation_elem_of_eq K f hgen hx' hfz₀,
    96	      ordZ_pointPullbackUnit K f hgen hz₀ hx' hfz₀, toAdd_ofAdd]
    97	  have hD : Scheme.presentationDivisor K
    98	      (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation
    99	      = Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hz₀ 1 := by
   100	    refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.ext_coeffAt fun z hz => ?_
   101	    by_cases hzz : z = z₀
   102	    · subst hzz
   103	      rw [hcoeff z₀ hz, hc1]
   104	      exact (Scheme.CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self hz₀ 1).symm
   105	    · rw [hzero z hz hzz]
   106	      exact (Scheme.CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hz₀ hz hzz 1).symm
   107	  rw [hD, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hz₀ 1, one_mul,
   108	    residueDeg_eq_of_isIso K f hover z₀, hfz₀]
   109	
   110	variable [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (W.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   111	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (W.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   112	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   113	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   114	
   115	/-- The single-point case: an isomorphism preserves the degree of the class of a one-point
   116	divisor. -/
   117	private theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_picClass_single_of_isIso (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f]
   118	    (hover : f ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) = W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
   119	    (hgen : f.base (genericPoint W) = genericPoint X)
   120	    {x' : X} (hx' : x' ≠ genericPoint X) :
   121	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f
   122	        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx' 1)))
   123	      = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx' 1)) := by
   124	  have h1 : Scheme.CechPic.map f
   125	      (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx' 1))
   126	      = (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').picClass := by
   127	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_single K hx']
   128	    exact (Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback _ _ _).symm
   129	  have h2 : (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').picClass
   130	      = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
   131	          (pointPullbackEquations K f hgen hx').presentation) := by
   132	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor,
   133	      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
   134	  rw [h1, h2, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass,
   135	    deg_presentationDivisor_pointPullback_of_isIso K f hover hgen hx',
   136	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx' 1, one_mul]
   137	
   138	/-- **W7-B3, scheme-level engine**: the degree of a Čech Picard class is invariant under
   139	`CechPic.map` of an isomorphism of curve bundles over `Spec K` — for every isomorphism
   140	`f : W ⟶ X` over `Spec K` and every class `L` on `X`,
   141	
   142	`classDeg K (CechPic.map f L) = classDeg K L`.
   143	
   144	The E-iv-alg ladder with the transition replaced by an isomorphism: reduce along the
   145	surjective additive class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K` to one-point divisors, present the
   146	point class by the tracked point equations, pull the presentation back along `f`, and close
   147	with the degenerate fiber computation (single fiber point, coefficient `1` by `ord`
   148	transport along the stalk isomorphism, residue degree transported along the residue-field
   149	isomorphism). -/
   150	theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_of_isIso (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f]
   151	    (hover : f ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) = W ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
   152	    (L : X.CechPic) :
   153	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f L) = classDeg K L := by
   154	  have hgen : f.base (genericPoint W) = genericPoint X := genericPoint_eq_of_surjective f
   155	  obtain ⟨D, rfl⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
   156	  suffices h : ∀ g : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ,
   157	      classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K g))
   158	        = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K g) from h D
   159	  intro g
   160	  induction g using Finsupp.induction with
   161	  | zero =>
   162	    change classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f
   163	      (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (0 : X.CurveDivisor)))
   164	      = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (0 : X.CurveDivisor))
   165	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, map_one, classDeg_one, classDeg_one]
   166	  | single_add p b g hpg hb ih =>
   167	    have key : ∀ D : X.CurveDivisor,
   168	        classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K D))
   169	          = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K D) →
   170	        classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map f
   171	          (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + D)))
   172	          = classDeg K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
   173	            (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + D)) := by
   174	      intro D hD
   175	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, ← Scheme.picClass_single_zpow K p.2 b,
   176	        map_mul, map_zpow, classDeg_mul, classDeg_mul, classDeg_zpow, classDeg_zpow, hD,
   177	        classDeg_cechPicMap_picClass_single_of_isIso K f hover hgen p.2]
   178	    exact key g ih
   179	
   180	end Ladder
   181	
   182	/-! ## The keystone: the `Over`-category form -/
   183	
   184	section Keystone
   185	
   186	open Scheme
   187	
   188	/-- **W7-B3 keystone (`classDeg_map_iso`)** — the `deg-d5b` worksheet §3's named Wave-7
   189	lemma, in the pinned `Over`-category form (`informal/w7-worksheet.md` §D2 B-3): for an
   190	isomorphism `e : X ≅ Y` of curve bundles over one field `K` and every Čech Picard class
   191	`L` of `Y`, the contravariant transport preserves the degree,
   192	
   193	`classDeg K (CechPic.map e.hom.left L) = classDeg K L`.
   194	
   195	Consumed by W7-B4a (`degAt` matching) and W7-B4b (θ); closes EW-3. -/
   196	theorem classDeg_map_iso {K : Type u} [Field K] {X Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
   197	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom] [IsProper X.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible X.hom]
   198	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 Y.hom] [IsProper Y.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible Y.hom]
   199	    (e : X ≅ Y) (L : Y.left.CechPic) :
   200	    letI : X.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := .ofHom X.hom
   201	    letI : Y.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := .ofHom Y.hom
   202	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   203	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom)
   204	    haveI : QuasiCompact (X.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   205	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact X.hom)
   206	    haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.left.moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   207	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero X
   208	    haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   209	      moduleFinite_hModule_one X
   210	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   211	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 Y.hom)
   212	    haveI : QuasiCompact (Y.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   213	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact Y.hom)
   214	    haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.left.moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   215	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero Y
   216	    haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   217	      moduleFinite_hModule_one Y
   218	    classDeg K (Scheme.CechPic.map e.hom.left L) = classDeg K L := by
   219	  letI : X.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := .ofHom X.hom
   220	  letI : Y.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := .ofHom Y.hom
   221	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   222	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 X.hom)
   223	  haveI : QuasiCompact (X.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   224	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact X.hom)
   225	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.left.moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   226	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero X
   227	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   228	    moduleFinite_hModule_one X
   229	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   230	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 Y.hom)
   231	  haveI : QuasiCompact (Y.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   232	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact Y.hom)
   233	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.left.moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   234	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero Y
   235	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   236	    moduleFinite_hModule_one Y
   237	  haveI : IsIso e.hom.left := inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((Over.forget _).map e.hom))
   238	  exact classDeg_cechPicMap_of_isIso K e.hom.left (Over.w e.hom) L

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The degree on the relative Picard group over a field (gap G-D5(b), SB-5 descent gadgets)
    10	
    11	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a field extension `K` of `k`, the relative
    12	Picard group `relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase` quotients out the classes
    13	pulled back from `Spec K` — but `Spec K` is a one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is
    14	trivial (`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`) and `classDeg K` kills `picFromBase`
    15	(`classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase`).  The degree therefore descends to the relative
    16	Picard group:
    17	
    18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg K : Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ`, with the anchor
    19	  `relPicDeg_relPicMk : relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L`;
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` — **E-iv-alg descended to `relPic`**: the
    21	  relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of any `k`-algebra map of
    22	  field extensions, `relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x`.
    23	
    24	These are the two descent gadgets of `informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §4 SB-5; the `degAt`
    25	brick (SB-6) consumes `relPicDeg` and `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` verbatim — on a field
    26	representative `(K', y)` of an étale-locally-trivial class, the honest degree is
    27	`relPicDeg K' y`, well-defined across representatives by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap`.
    28	-/
    29	
    30	set_option autoImplicit false
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    35	
    36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    37	
    38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    39	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	
    41	/-! ## `classDeg` kills the classes from the base -/
    42	
    43	/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
    44	one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
    45	trivial. -/
    46	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    47	    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
    48	    classDeg K L = 0 := by
    49	  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
    50	  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
    51	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
    52	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]
    53	
    54	/-! ## The relative degree -/
    55	
    56	/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
    57	gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
    58	`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
    59	one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
    60	field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
    61	noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    62	    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
    63	  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
    64	    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
    65	      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
    66	      (fun L hL => by
    67	        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
    68	        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
    69	        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
    70	        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))
    71	
    72	/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
    73	`classDeg K L`. -/
    74	@[simp]
    75	theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    76	    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
    77	    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
    78	  rfl
    79	
    80	/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
    81	gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
    82	map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
    83	depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
    84	theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
    85	    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
    86	    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
    87	  induction x using relPic.ind with
    88	  | mk L =>
    89	    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
    90	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
    91	          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
    92	      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
    93	    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
    94	      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]
    95	
    96	end AlgebraicGeometry

import Mathlib
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FGAPicRepresentability

/-!
# Degree slices of the relative-divisor functor + the degree-refined Abel map

Campaign milestones **D1'** (degree-`d` divisor functor `DivFunctorDeg`, clopen
degree decomposition, base-change stability of the fibre degree) and **A2**
(degree-refined Abel map `abelDeg`) of the `instHasPicScheme` campaign
(`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`), on top of the landed divisor
functor `Scheme.DivFunctor` (Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:div`;
`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`).

## The fibre degree

For a family of relative effective divisors `x : DivFamily π T` (the quotient
encoding: `q : O_{X_T} ↠ F = O_D` with invertible kernel ideal `I_D = ker q`),
the **fibre degree** at `t : T` is

  `x.fiberDeg t := dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t}) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ((X_T)_t, F_t)`,

Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`'s degree of the fibre divisor `D_t ⊆ X_t` — the
`H⁰`-only, cohomology-free rank.

**AUDIT (encoding choice, D1').** The campaign phrase "rank-`d` of the
finite-flat pushforward of `O_D`" is realized by its *pointwise shadow*: the
in-tree substrate has no `q_* O_D`-as-locally-free-object (that is exactly the
B3 rigid-pushforward engine, unbuilt), and for a finite flat family the rank of
the pushforward at `t` *equals* `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(D_t, O_{D_t})` (pushforward along
an affine morphism is exact and commutes with base change).  The fibre-section
form is honest at full generality (any `π`, any `T`; `Module.finrank` junk
value `0` if the fibre sections are infinite-dimensional, which does not occur
for divisor fibres in the relative-curve regime) and is what Kleiman's
`deg D_t` means.  When B3 lands, `q_* O_D` is locally free of rank
`fiberDeg` and the two vocabularies fuse.

**AUDIT (base change, D1').** `fiberDeg` is stable under arbitrary base change
`ψ : T' ⟶ T` (`fiberDeg_pullbackAlong`): the fibre of `X_{T'}/T'` at `t'` is
the base change of the fibre of `X_T/T` at `t = ψ(t')` along the residue
extension `κ(t) → κ(t')`, and `H⁰` of a finitely presented module with proper
support commutes with base field extension (Stacks 02KH at `i = 0`).  This is
proved **axiom-clean** from the twist-free Γ-fibre core
`Scheme.finrank_gammaTop_baseChange_of_hasProperSupport`
(`Picard/SchematicSupport.lean`) — NOT from the twisted engine
`Scheme.hilbertFunction_quotBaseMap` (`Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean`), which
still rests on the sorried tensor–pullback leaf
`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso`.  At `m = 0` no twist is needed, so the
degree lane stays sorry-free (recon correction to the campaign plan's
"the 02KE/02KH engine is landed" — only its untwisted core is).

## The clopen degree decomposition — honest form

**AUDIT (coproduct pin, D1').** The naive presheaf-level statement
"`DivFunctor = ⨿_d DivFunctorDeg d`" is FALSE: on a disconnected `T` a family
with non-constant fibre degree lies in no degree piece, and at `T = ∅` every
piece contains the (unique) empty family, so the pieces are not disjoint.  The
honest pins delivered here are:

* every `T`-point decomposes `T` into clopen constant-degree pieces
  (`DivFamily.degLocus`, `DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_pullbackAlong_degLocusHom`,
  `DivFamily.iSup_degLocus`, `DivFamily.degLocus_disjoint`) — this is the form
  the coproduct assembly `G4` (`hom_sigma_decompose`) consumes;
* on a nonempty preconnected `T` the canonical comparison
  `Σ_d (DivFunctorDeg π d)(T) → DivFunctor π (T)` is a bijection
  (`divFunctorDeg_sigma_bijective`);
* degree pieces of a common class agree (`DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg.unique`,
  nonempty `T`).

The only non-formal input is **Zariski-local constancy of the fibre degree**.
This is TRUE in the campaign regime (relative curve: `D → T` is
proper + quasi-finite, hence finite, and a finitely presented `T`-flat module
with finite support has finite locally free pushforward — Mumford, *Abelian
Varieties* II §5; Kleiman §3 Ex. `ex:DivC`) but is NOT derivable from the
current in-tree substrate (it needs the finite/rank half of the B3 pushforward
engine plus `D_t` finite from relative dimension 1).  Following the house gate
pattern (`HasPicScheme`), it is pinned as the instance-free Prop-class
`HasLocallyConstantDivDeg C` at the AJC curve regime, and every decomposition
statement is ALSO provided in hypothesis-parametrized form (an explicit
`IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` argument), so the eventual discharge is a
one-line instance.  We deliberately do NOT state the gate for general `π`:
for relative dimension `≥ 2` the fibre rank of `O_{D_t}` can jump (only `χ` is
locally constant), which is why Kleiman filters `Div` by Hilbert polynomials in
general and by the degree only over curves.

## The degree ledger and the Abel-map sign (A2)

**Sign convention (audit item 7-half).** The Abel map is
`abelMapWitness C = abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, i.e.

  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  —

a divisor family maps to the *negative* of the class of its ideal sheaf
(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:461`).  The degree-refined Abel map
`abelDeg C d : divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C` is the restriction of
`abelMapWitness` along the degree-`d` inclusion; its defining property is
`abelDeg_app_mk`.  It deliberately lands in `picSharp C` — carving out
`picSharpDeg C d` is milestone B4, not this file.

**AUDIT (degree-coherence vocabulary, A2).** "The ideal sheaf `ker q` of a
rank-`d` family has fibre degree `−d`" is stated in the **rank (colength)
vocabulary** — the strongest honestly-provable form today: the χ-ledger
(`deg = χ(I) − χ(O)`, campaign P3) is unbuilt, and the adelic
`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor` degree cannot yet be attached to the sheaf-theoretic
line bundle `ker q` on a family fibre (that needs the `M ≅ O(div s)`
regular-section bricks, also P3).  What IS proved, per fibre `t`:

* the ideal restricts to the fibre: the kernel–pullback comparison
  `(I_D)_t ≅ ker(q_t)` is an isomorphism (`DivFamily.fiberKernelIso`) and the
  fibre ideal inclusion `(I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t}` stays monic
  (`DivFamily.mono_fiber_kernel_ι`) with `(I_D)_t` invertible
  (`DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel`) — `D_t ⊆ X_t` is an honest
  effective Cartier divisor (Kleiman §3, note after Def. `df:div`);
* its colength is the degree: `O_{X_t}/(I_D)_t ≅ (O_D)_t`
  (`DivFamily.fiberCokernelIso`), so
  `dim_{κ(t)} Γ(coker((I_D)_t ↪ O_{X_t})) = fiberDeg x t = d`

36	## Decisions identified
37	
38	The directive bundles two distinct decisions:
39	
40	1. **What is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` definitionally?** Identity-component (Stacks
41	   04KU/04KV) vs degree-zero open-and-closed subscheme (Kleiman
42	   `thm:Pphifin` + `ex:curves`)?
43	2. **Is there a Mathlib idiom for "kernel of a group-scheme
44	   morphism"** that the project should use directly?
45	
46	### Decision 1: Underlying scheme of `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
47	
48	- **Mathlib idiom**: NEITHER `IdentityComponent` of a group scheme NOR
49	  `ker(deg)` of a morphism of group schemes exists in Mathlib b80f227.
50	  Mathlib has `MonoidHom.ker` (sets / `Subgroup G`) but no
51	  scheme-level `GrpObj.ker`. Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel`
52	  requires `HasZeroMorphisms`, which `Scheme` does not satisfy
53	  (`Scheme` is cartesian-monoidal, not abelian). The **literature**
54	  has two equivalent definitions for smooth-proper-curve targets:
55	  Kleiman `prp:pic0` (identity component) and Kleiman
56	  `ex:curves` + Milne III.1 p.~87 (kernel of degree = `Pic⁰=Pic^0`).
57	- **Project's current path**: Identity-component via Stacks 04KU/04KV
58	  (parked, ~350 LOC pending Mathlib upstream `Stacks 037Q` /
59	  `04KV`).
60	- **Gap**: divergent-with-cost. The identity-component definition
61	  requires building project-side or upstream Mathlib infrastructure
62	  (`LocallyConnectedSpace` for locally-Noetherian schemes;
63	  `geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section`; descent of clopen
64	  partitions along fpqc base change). The degree-stratification
65	  definition only requires Kleiman §6 `thm:Pphifin` (the Hilbert-
66	  polynomial open-and-closed decomposition) and the curve-specific
67	  identification "leading coefficient of Hilbert polynomial = degree"
68	  (Riemann–Roch, RR.1).
69	- **Cost of divergence (current shipped path)**:
70	  - 2 typed sorries in `IdentityComponent.lean` (`geometricallyConnected_of_connected_of_section`,
71	    `IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` iso slot) waiting on Stacks
72	    037Q / 04KV substrate not in Mathlib b80f227.
73	  - 1 typed sorry in `IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism`
74	    needing EGA IV₂ 4.5.8 (smooth × geom-conn → conn) + Stacks 04KU.
75	  - 1 typed sorry in `IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
76	    needing the group-translation argument (EGA IV₂ 4.5.8/4.6.1).
77	  - Phase A.3.i parked at ~0/iter for 4 iters; ~350 LOC of
78	    Mathlib-upstream-grade work remaining.
79	- **Verdict**: **STRUCTURAL_OK** (pivot recommended).
80	
81	### Decision 2: Mathlib kernel idiom for `f : G → H` of group schemes
82	
83	- **Mathlib idiom**: No direct idiom. The category-theoretic shape
84	  ("kernel of a group-object morphism in a finite-limit category") is
85	  the pullback `pullback f (e_H ∘ !) : ker f ⟶ G`, where
86	  `e_H : 𝟙_C ⟶ H` is the identity of the target group object and
87	  `!` is the unique map to the terminal. Mathlib supports this
88	  IMPLICITLY via `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks` on schemes, but
89	  does not package `GrpObj.ker` as a named construction.
90	  Closest precedents:
91	  - `MonoidHom.ker` (`Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Ker`): plain
92	    group homomorphism in Type, returns `Subgroup G`. Not applicable
93	    at scheme level.
94	  - `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker`
95	    (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Basic`): kernel ideal
96	    sheaf of a scheme morphism, i.e. `Y.IdealSheafData` not a
97	    `Scheme`. A different concept (set-theoretic preimage of zero
98	    section, not the categorical fiber over the identity element).
99	  - `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel`: requires `HasZeroMorphisms`, not
100	    applicable to `Scheme` or `Over (Spec k)`.
101	  - `MonoidHom.fiberEquivKer`: the categorical insight (kernel =
102	    fiber over identity), but in Type only.
103	- **Project's natural reframing**: The directive's "Pic⁰ := ker(deg)"
104	  framing is conceptual. The PRACTICAL construction is the
105	  degree-stratification:
106	  `PicScheme C = ∐_{d∈ℤ} Pic^d C` (Kleiman `ex:curves`), with
107	  `Pic⁰ := Pic^0` the degree-0 open-and-closed subscheme. This sidesteps
108	  the categorical-pullback definition entirely.
109	- **Gap**: NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL (categorical `GrpObj.ker`) but with
110	  workaround: the degree-stratification gives the kernel directly,
111	  without invoking pullback-of-identity. The kernel is the union of
112	  connected components mapping to `0 ∈ ℤ`, and in the discrete
113	  codomain case this is just the preimage of an open-and-closed
114	  point.
115	- **Verdict**: **NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL** for the abstract idiom, but
116	  not on the critical path: the project does not need to invoke a
117	  generic kernel construction, only the curve-specific
118	  decomposition. The "ker(deg)" framing in the directive should be
119	  read as a NAMING / MATHEMATICAL JUSTIFICATION for the degree-0
120	  component, not as a literal `kernel.lift` / `pullback.lift`
121	  invocation.
122	
123	## Confirmation of the equivalence "ker(deg) = identity component"
124	
125	### Kleiman §6, `ex:curves` (lines 4665–4681 of `references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`)
126	
127	> *Assume $X/S$ is locally projective over $S$ and flat, and its
128	> geometric fibers are integral curves. Given an integer $m$, let
129	> $\Pic^m_{X/S} \subset \Pic_{X/S}$ be the set of points representing
130	> invertible sheaves $\mathcal L$ of degree $m$. Show the $\Pic^m_{X/S}$
131	> are open and closed subschemes of finite type; show they are
132	> disjoint and cover; and show that forming them commutes with
133	> changing $S$.*
134	>
135	> *Show there is no abuse of notation: the fiber of $\Pic^0_{X/S}$
136	> over $s\in S$ is the connected component of $0\in\Pic_{X_s/k_s}$.
137	> Show there is no torsion: $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$. Show each
138	> $\Pic^m_{X/S}$ is an fppf-torsor under $\Pic^0_{X/S}$.*
139	
140	This is the **direct citation** for `ker(deg) = identity component` on
141	smooth proper geometrically integral curves: the degree-0 component IS
142	the connected component of the identity. The project's curve hypotheses
143	(`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom + IsProper C.hom + GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`)
144	satisfy Kleiman's setup.
145	
146	### Milne III.1 (PDF p.~93 / book p.~87)
147	
148	> *Let $\Pic^r(C)$ be the set of divisor classes of degree $r$. For
149	> a fixed point $P_0$ on $C$, the map $[D]\mapsto[D+rP_0]:
150	> \Pic^0(C)\to\Pic^r(C)$ is a bijection **(both $\Pic^0(C)$ and
151	> $\Pic^r(C)$ are fibres of the map $\deg : \Pic(C)\to\Z$)**.*
152	
153	And p.~88:
154	> *We write $\Pic^0(C)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of
155	> invertible sheaves of degree zero on $C$.*
156	
157	This is the **textbook definition of `Pic⁰` for a curve**: kernel of
158	the degree map. Milne's Theorem 1.6 then says this functor `P_C^0` is
159	represented by an abelian variety (the Jacobian), with no detour
160	through identity-component theory at all.
161	
162	### Kleiman §6 `rmk:curves` (line 4682)
163	
164	> *There is another important case where $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$,
165	> namely, when $X$ is an Abelian $S$-scheme. [...]*
166	
167	Confirms the identification also holds in the abelian-scheme case
168	(used downstream when iterating to `Pic⁰` of `Pic⁰`).
169	
170	**Conclusion**: The equivalence `ker(deg) = identity component` is
171	mathematically standard, explicitly cited in both primary sources
172	(Kleiman) and the project's secondary reference (Milne). For the
173	project's curve hypothesis it is provable from Kleiman §6 alone,
174	WITHOUT invoking 04KU / 04KV.
175	
176	## Recommendation
177	
178	**Pivot to ker(deg)-style Pic⁰ via the degree-stratification**, with
179	concrete plan:
180	
181	1. **Repurpose `IdentityComponent.lean`** (or split into two files).
182	   The abstract `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` substrate can stay
183	   for future use (no urgency to close its sorries — those are
184	   pure-Mathlib upstream-grade lemmas).
185	
186	2. **Add Kleiman `ex:curves` decomposition** as the substrate.
187	   Sketch (using Mathlib b80f227 instances `inferInstance` shape):
188	   ```lean

190	   of a smooth proper geom integral curve, as an open-and-closed

202	   ```

204	3. **Redefine `Pic0Scheme C := PicScheme.degComp C 0`** in
205	   `IdentityComponent.lean` (or new file `Picard/Pic0ByDegree.lean`).
206	   The TYPE remains `Over (Spec k)`, so downstream consumers in

208	   ABI-unchanged.

210	4. **Inherit `GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)`** from the multiplication on
211	   `PicScheme C`: `deg(L ⊗ M) = deg L + deg M`, so `Pic^0 × Pic^0 →

217	   `Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` in `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`)

219	   (Kleiman `prp:pic0`), but with the pivot:
220	   - The statement no longer blocks the **definition** of `Pic⁰` or
221	     its downstream `Pic^0`-torsor structure.
222	   - The substrate "`Pic^0` connected over `k̄`" can be deferred or

224	   - Or, in characteristic zero, derived from `Pic^τ` finiteness +

242	### Estimated cost of pivot
243	
244	| Component | LOC | Status |
245	|---|---|---|
246	| Kleiman `thm:Pphifin` / `ex:curves` decomposition of `PicScheme` | ~80–150 | A.3.vii substrate (gated) |
247	| `Pic0Scheme C := PicScheme.degComp C 0` | ~10 | trivial |
248	| Open-and-closed inclusion `Pic^0 ↪ PicScheme` | ~10 | trivial |

252	
253	### Net effect on Route A iter budget
254	
255	- Identity-component path (parked): 4 iters elapsed at 0/it, ~350 LOC
256	  outstanding with substrate-unowned Mathlib gaps (Stacks 037Q,
257	  04KU/04KV). Best-case ~20+ iters; risk of unbounded park.
258	- Pivot path: ~6–10 iters (under Cartier route assumption for A.3.vii
259	  substrate ~3–5 iters + Pic⁰ assembly ~3–5 iters). Critical
260	  Mathlib gap is Hilbert-polynomial open-and-closed decomposition
261	  (Kleiman `thm:Pphifin`), which the project ALREADY plans to build
262	  for A.3.vii regardless.
263	
264	The pivot saves an estimated **10–18 iters** and removes the
265	unbounded-park risk on Stacks 04KU/04KV.
266	
267	### Caveat — the geometric-irreducibility theorem still needs care
268	
269	`Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` in `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` is the
270	ONE downstream statement where the identity-component substrate
271	matters intrinsically: Kleiman `prp:pic0` proves
272	`Pic⁰ geometrically irreducible` precisely because it is the
273	connected component of the identity (in a smooth group scheme,
274	connected components are irreducible). Under the degree-stratification
275	definition, the geom-irreducibility of `Pic^0` is NOT immediate — it
276	still needs to be shown that `Pic^0` (= degree-0 component) is
277	connected, which IS the content of Stacks 04KU once you have a
278	section.

281	- Geometric irreducibility no longer BLOCKS the definition of
282	  `Pic⁰` or the bulk of downstream construction.
283	- It is needed only at the assembly stage (`Pic0.isAbelianVariety`),
284	  and can be attacked in isolation with the same Stacks 04KU
285	  substrate (or finessed via `Pic^τ` finiteness in characteristic 0).
286	- The other three conjuncts of "abelian variety" (smooth, proper,
287	  `GrpObj`) are independent and proceed via the pivot definition.
288	
289	This is a partial decoupling, not a full elimination. But it converts
290	the Stacks 04KU dependency from "blocks the whole positive-genus
291	arm" to "blocks one of four conjuncts of the assembly statement",
292	which is a strict improvement.
293	
294	### When the pivot might be wrong
295	
296	The pivot would be REJECTED if:
297	- Downstream consumers depend on `Pic0Scheme` being defined as
298	  `IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` ABI (none do — confirmed by
299	  reading `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` and `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`).

301	  (then `Pic^0 ≠ Pic⁰` is possible; cf. Kleiman `eg:Pphifin` for
302	  disjoint-lines). Project hypothesis is fixed.
303	- Mathlib were to ship 04KU/04KV imminently (low probability —
304	  no PR visible at b80f227).
